Subject: Dedicated vs Private (VPC) — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Tim / Anna —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed around data isolation and deployment mode. High-level: FinSecure's initial requirement is that customer data never leaves their control plane/network for PII and transaction logs; Hosted API is likely not acceptable unless we can guarantee complete data plane separation (which we generally don't for hosted multi-tenant).

Notes from the call:
- Primary requirement: Strong data isolation for PII / transaction analytics.
- Options we covered: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) vs Private (VPC / on-prem).
- Questions you asked: whether logs/metrics ever traverse Redwood-managed networks, KMS/HSM integration, and timeline for on-prem deployment.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) I'll share a short SOC 2 summary and an architecture draft that shows the Private VPC control/data plane split.
2) Mateo to provide a technical note on what Dedicated isolation looks like (networking, logging, support access).
3) Schedule a security deep-dive next week with your security architect to walk the details (KMS, audit logs, retention). Suggested times: Thu 6/3 10:00am PT or Fri 6/4 9:00am PT — what works best?

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, architecture-vpc-draft.png, DPA-draft.docx

I'll follow up with the attachments in a separate email thread from Mateo with the technical details.

Best,

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. A couple clarifying points from our side: we operate under fairly strict controls around egress and key management. Specifically:

- We need confirmation that no plaintext PII or transaction logs leave our VPC in any deployment option.
- For Dedicated: we understand compute is isolated, but are there any control-plane calls (telemetry, health checks) that would route through Redwood-managed endpoints? If so, what data is included?
- KMS requirement: customer-managed keys are mandatory (HSM-backed preferable).
- Logging/monitoring: we need audit logs retained for 5 years in our account or exported to our SIEM; is there an option to ship logs only to our endpoints?

We can do the security deep-dive on Thu 6/3 10:00am PT. Please send calendar invite and an agenda; Anna and I will have our security engineer join.

Also please include estimated timelines and the procurement path for Private/on-prem if we decide to go that route — we typically need architecture review and legal sign-off for on-prem deployments.

Thanks,
Tim Jenkins
Security Lead | FinSecure

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private (VPC) — technical clarifications

Hi Tim — following up with the technical details you asked for. Short version first, then specifics.

Summary:
- Dedicated (Reserved Capacity): compute is single-tenant at the GPU pool level; control plane (scheduling/experiments/telemetry) is Redwood-managed but can be configured to minimize telemetry. Customer data processed by the model may be kept in ephemeral RAM and KV caches; persistent storage/logs can be configured to be forwarded only to customer endpoints. No data is written to multi-tenant object stores by default.
- Private (VPC / On-prem): control plane remains in Redwood (unless you opt for the Private control-plane offering), but the data plane can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem. In that mode, we support VPC peering / private link and optional on-prem appliance. Customer-managed KMS (HSM) integrations supported for key operations.

Technical answers to your bullets:
- Plaintext PII leaving VPC: Private VPC or on-prem are the only modes where we can guarantee that processed data and logs remain in your network. Dedicated reduces cross-tenant exposure but control-plane telemetry may still traverse Redwood endpoints unless specific telemetry filters are applied and contractually enforced.
- Control-plane calls: for Dedicated we currently send health and scheduling pings to Redwood-managed endpoints; payloads are limited to service/instance identifiers and non-PII telemetry. We can provide a telemetry schema and negotiate suppression of optional fields.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can integrate with external HSM providers for Private/on-prem. Key material never leaves the customer-managed KMS.
- Logs export: we can forward logs via secure push to your SIEM (syslog/HTTPS) or you can pull logs from an S3 bucket in your account that we populate. Retention policy is configurable; we can support a 5-year export/retention via your account.

I'll attach a short architecture diagram that shows the Private VPC data plane and the Dedicated flow. Also attaching a SOC 2 summary for your security team.

Proposed next steps:
- Security deep-dive Thu 6/3 10:00am PT (Marissa to send invite).
- Post-deep-dive: we can run a short POC in Dedicated mode to validate latency and KV cache behavior (2-3 weeks), or start architecture reviews for Private/on-prem (3-6 weeks prep + on-prem lead time).

Thanks — happy to go into any of these in the call.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
